title: AI Isn’t Saving You Minutes — It’s Collapsing Months

segments.text: A single systematic literature review takes nine to eighteen months. AI can collapse it to hours. Yet most time-management advice is still about rearranging your calendar.

Here is what the credible research actually shows. A 2026 preprint reports this manual workflow costs over a hundred thousand dollars per review. The authors compressed it to minutes or hours through an AI-assisted review pipeline. A 2025 paper in NEJM AI found that human-plus-AI review pipelines significantly accelerated peer review quality assessment. And Nature itself has asked whether hidden costs come with that speed — a fair caveat. But these tools do not exist in five years. They exist now. If you read reports, review documents, or synthesise research, AI can compress what takes you a month into a single afternoon. The question is whether you will be the person who uses them — or the one they replace.
Subscribe now. Next week I show you exactly how. If you spend even one hour a week processing information — that button is where you start reclaiming it.

key_points.text: AI’s real productivity leverage is not marginal calendar optimisation but collapsing multi-month analytical workflows into hours — a finding grounded in the most rigorous domain of academic research.
